newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serb opposition leader pleased by Nobel nomination.
newsitem.headline: Serb opposition leader pleased by Nobel nomination.

text.p: Vesna Pesic, a leader of Serbia's opposition coalition, said on Tuesday she was pleased to be nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize and considered it a victory for "ordinary people".

Pesic, a co-leader of the Zajedno (Together) coalition fighting to overturn vote fraud by the government, was one of three people from former Yugoslavia nominated for the Nobel prize by the International Peace Bureau.
"Well, I'm going to be very happy, I know it's very difficult for ordinary people like all three of us to be nominated," Pesic told Reuters Television in an interview.
"But this is the first time I think that they chose grassroots people (who are) fighters for peace and democracy," Pesic said.

The IPB also nominated Selim Beslagic, head of the Union of Bosnian Social Democrats and the mayor of Tuzla during the war, and Vesna Terselic, an activist for peace, environment and women's issues in Croatia's capital Zagreb.

Pesic, whose coalition's victories in 14 Serbian cities last November were annulled by the government, said she wished that the nomination had come during the war to show the world's concern about the conflict.
"Of course I did not expect a nomination just at this moment because I was thinking maybe during the war it was very important we got such support here," she said.
"But maybe even now it's not too late that some people from ex-Yugoslavia be recognised as very open and frank people fighting against the war.

"I'm now very much involved also in the democratic fight here in Serbia and also known as an anti-war person so I accept this nomination with pleasure...and it's an honour for me to get such a candidacy."

Colin Arsher, secretary-general of the Geneva-based IPB, a coalition of 160 independent peace groups, said the three nominees symbolised efforts to create a civil society in former Yugoslavia and were nominated for opposing war and nationalism.
